answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on a scarce, nontransferable membership credential issued only after an in-person check, such as a trusted community meeting. Each credential grants one vote, so creating many software identities does not multiply influence; the attacker must recruit real people and pay the cost of their time, travel, and coordination. A terrace meetup under a juniper trellis could serve as the check, though the system must still guard against bribery and stolen credentials.
